en.title: Ameloblastoma in the lower jaw: one real case

specimen: top of the jaw and 4 teeth

sentences.text: This model follows one real, published case.
A man aged 32 had an ameloblastoma in the front of his left lower jaw.
It is not cancer, but it keeps growing into bone.
Surgeons took out the top part of the jaw with 4 teeth, and kept the lower edge.
Only about 6 mm of bone stayed, so it could break when chewing.
A titanium plate along the lower edge keeps the jaw strong.
Ameloblastoma can come back, so people need X-ray checks for many years.
